source_fragment_refinements.before: Senate 100055 separately establishes the named Bridging Immigration-related Deficits Experienced Nationwide Reimbursement Fund within DOJ. The AG shall use its amounts for grants to eligible States, State agencies and local-government units pursuant to their existing statutory authorities, for the complete listed purposes. Locating/apprehending under paragraph (1) requires both a crime under federal, State or local law and unlawful U.S. presence. Paragraph (7) vehicle/logistics/transport/other support is provided by a State agency to law-enforcement agencies for locating/apprehending persons with that same crime-plus-unlawful-presence pair. Paragraph (6) funds transporting aliens described in paragraph (1) within the United States to locations related to their apprehension, detention and prosecution. The pair is not imported into every other purpose, and unlawful presence alone is not treated as the required additional crime. Other listed purposes are domestic investigative-information collection/analysis against gang or other criminal activity; investigating/prosecuting crimes committed by aliens within the United States and domestic drug/human-trafficking crimes; court operations related to prosecution of crimes committed by aliens or drug and human trafficking crimes, without a repeated within-the-United-States phrase in that separate paragraph; and temporary criminal detention of aliens. Temporary criminal detention is not generic civil-immigration detention. Existing-authority wording does not itself grant new State arrest/removal powers or determine any individual crime/status.
source_fragment_refinements.after: Senate 100055 separately establishes the Bridging Immigration-related Deficits Experienced Nationwide (BIDEN) Reimbursement Fund within the Department of Justice. The Attorney General shall use the Fund amounts for grants to eligible States, State agencies, and units of local government, pursuant to their existing statutory authorities. The paragraph 1 purpose is locating and apprehending aliens who have committed a crime under Federal, State, or local law, in addition to being unlawfully present in the United States. The paragraph 2 purpose is collection and analysis of law enforcement investigative information within the United States to counter gang or other criminal activity. The paragraph 3 purpose is investigating and prosecuting crimes committed by aliens within the United States and drug and human trafficking crimes committed within the United States. The paragraph 4 purpose is court operations related to the prosecution of crimes committed by aliens and drug and human trafficking crimes. The paragraph 5 purpose is temporary criminal detention of aliens. The paragraph 6 purpose is transporting aliens described in paragraph (1) within the United States to locations related to the apprehension, detention, and prosecution of such aliens. The paragraph 7 purpose is vehicle maintenance, logistics, transportation, and other support provided to law enforcement agencies by a State agency to enhance the ability to locate and apprehend aliens who have committed crimes under Federal, State, or local law, in addition to being unlawfully present in the United States. Paragraphs (1) and (7) retain their own additional-crime and unlawful-presence requirements; paragraph (6) retains the paragraph (1) person category, its domestic transport limit and its destination purposes. Those requirements are not imported into the other purposes. Temporary criminal detention is distinct from civil immigration detention. Court paragraph (4) prints no separate within-the-United-States phrase; no neighboring location condition is borrowed. Listed conjunctions report the source categories, not a determination that a particular grant must fund both crime categories. Existing statutory authorities do not create new State arrest/removal powers or establish actual crime/status/expense eligibility.
